ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image there are four circular containers of the same size, labeled from left to right as H2O, CH4, Ne, and He. The question states that these identical containers each contain the same amount of substance of different gases at 298 K, so the container volume, temperature, and amount of substance of gas are the same; if according to ideal gas behavior, the pressures would be the same. Now not assuming ideal behavior, the pressure differences mainly come from intermolecular forces. In real gases, intermolecular attractions make the effective pressure of gas collisions with the container walls decrease. H2O is a polar molecule and can form strong hydrogen bonds; CH4, Ne, and He are all nonpolar particles, mainly having only weaker dispersion forces. Therefore H2O has the strongest intermolecular attractions, the actual pressure decreases the most, so the one with the lowest pressure is H2O.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: four equal circular containers are labeled H2O, CH4, Ne, and He. From the text, note that each container has the same number of moles at 298 K and identical volume, so any pressure difference must come from nonideal behavior. Compare intermolecular attractions among the gases. H2O molecules are polar and hydrogen-bond strongly, while CH4, Ne, and He are nonpolar with only dispersion forces. Since attractive forces lower real-gas pressure relative to ideal behavior, select the gas with the strongest attractions: H2O.
method.CoT_raw: 图像中有四个大小相同的圆形容器，从左到右分别标有 H2O、CH4、Ne 和 He。题目说明这些相同容器在 298 K 下各装有相同物质的量的不同气体，因此容器体积、温度和气体物质的量相同；若按理想气体行为，压力会相同。现在不假设理想行为，压力差主要来自分子间作用力。真实气体中，分子间吸引力会使气体对容器壁的碰撞有效压力降低。H2O 是极性分子且能形成强氢键；CH4、Ne 和 He 都是非极性粒子，主要只有较弱的色散力。因此 H2O 的分子间吸引力最强，实际压力降低最多，所以压力最低的是 H2O。

Apply a real-gas equation concept such as the van der Waals equation: the ideal pressure would be the same for all, but attractions subtract a term proportional to the gas's attraction parameter. planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the van der Waals form P = nRT/(V - nb) - a(n/V)^2. At fixed n, V, and T, the attraction parameter a lowers pressure, while the excluded-volume parameter b tends to raise it. Water has a much larger effective attraction parameter/condensability because of hydrogen bonding than methane, neon, or helium, so its negative pressure correction is greatest and dominates for this comparison.
